messages:
nimbus_ops: Hey Redwood, NimbusApps hitting a spike of 502/504s across eu-west and us-east when calling hosted /v1/chat. Started ~09:04 UTC after a large load test. Example header: X-Req-Id: nimbus-20260306-09. Response is often \"HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\" with empty body.

nimbus_ops: repro curl we used:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"X-Req-Id: nimbus-20260306-09\" -d @payload.json \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat\"
```

alex_sre: Looking at edge/ingress right now. Envoy is logging a ton of \"upstream premature EOF\" and \"connection timeout\" entries. A pattern: upstream socket close without a 5xx body. Also some downstream 504s when Envoy waited past cluster timeout.

alex_sre: Cluster config note: our default cluster max_connections is 2048 and max_pending_requests 2048. Under the client's bursty simultaneous streams we saw per-host connection exhaustion -> new streams get refused/short-circuited.

maria_runtime: Runtime telemetry: several GPU workers hit OOM and were SIGKILL'ed while writing outputs for very long contexts (avg prompt ~8k-12k tokens). Logs show: 
```
ERROR infer_engine: process 12345 killed by signal 9; reason: OutOfMemory while allocating KV cache
stack: ...
```
The processes drop the socket immediately; nothing returns to Envoy, so it surfaces as 502.

tony_oncall: @maria_runtime can you confirm whether the runtime returns a 5xx before exit or just dies? Need to know if envoys sees reset vs HTTP error.

maria_runtime: It dies (SIGKILL). No clean 5xx response. So envoy reports upstream reset/premature EOF.

alex_sre: Ok that maps to the 502s. The 504s are from requests queued at envoy waiting >30s for backend response when cluster was at capacity. Client reported ~900 rps with many long-lived streams.

nimbus_ops: Repro steps from our ops: 1) Spin 300 workers at 3 streams each (~900 concurrent requests) 2) Send 8k-12k token messages 3) Observe intermittent 502/504 within 2-5 minutes. Can reproduce reliably if we sustain for 3+ minutes.

alex_sre: Immediate mitigations we recommended to Nimbus: 1) throttle concurrency per client process 2) implement exponential backoff with jitter on 502/504 3) route large-context requests to smaller model variant temporarily.

maria_runtime: Medium-term runtime fixes: - Add soft admission control to reject extremely large contexts when node memory is above threshold (return 422 with guidance) - Add a small graceful-kill path to return 5xx instead of hard socket drop where possible - Tune docker memory + OOM killer behavior. New canary image: redwood/runtime:v2026-03-06-oom-guard-2

alex_sre: For edge: I pushed a canary envoy config to bump cluster.max_connections -> 8192 and reduce max_pending_requests to 1024 for the inference cluster on canary hosts. Also extended upstream idle timeouts slightly.

deploy-bot: deploy started: envoy-config/cluster-bump -> canary-host-3

tony_oncall: Canary synthesized load for 10 minutes with the client's repro and the canary host had no upstream premature EOFs. CPU/mem steady.

maria_runtime: Launched runtime canary (oom-guard-2) to 5% of runtime pool. Under simulated long contexts it returned controlled 422s when the admission control threshold was crossed. That prevented SIGKILLs on the canary nodes.

jen: I told NimbusApps support to pause aggressive bursts for 20 minutes while we roll mitigations. Also told them we will investigate billing credit for failed requests during the window.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-06-edge-502-504-nimbus, severity: P2

alex_sre: Roll plan: 1) roll envoy cluster config region-by-region over 30-40m 2) ramp runtime canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over next hour 3) update developer docs + SDK snippets with recommended retry/backoff and model-fallback patterns for long contexts 4) add an alert for runtime OOM kill rate crossing threshold.

tony_oncall: I'll own the postmortem. Initial RCA: combination of high-concurrency long-context requests causing runtime OOMs (hard kills) + Envoy per-cluster connection/pending limits -> upstream socket closures (502) and queued timeouts (504).

nimbus_ops: We paused. Will resume when you give the all-clear and will keep load low in the meantime.

alex_sre: After the first wave of rollouts Nimbus resumed a 15-minute test run at original load profile and reported no 502/504s. They saw far fewer connection resets in their client logs.

nimbus_ops: Confirmed stable for 15m so far. We'll monitor for 24h and report anything odd. Thanks for the quick triage.

maria_runtime: Follow-ups: PR to add prompt-length admission control, soft-exit path for memory pressure, and automated e2e test for large-token bursts.

alex_sre: Ops follow-ups: update edge playbook to include cluster limits for inference clusters, add simulation harness for high-concurrency large-context workloads, and validate env timeout settings across all regions.

jen: Support action: create billing ticket to credit failed requests in the incident window. We'll close once postmortem and billing ticket are complete. Great work :thumbsup:

-- end of thread --
